Thanks — I ran the numbers against our SLA policy. Summary:

Facts
- Reported outage window (customer): 2027-06-18 22:40 -> 2027-06-19 02:10 UTC (~3.5 hours)
- Verified outage (Redwood monitoring): 2027-06-18 22:45 -> 2027-06-19 02:08 UTC (~3.38 hours)
- Billing period: calendar month; average monthly invoice used for estimate: $121,500

Policy / Calc (standard SLA offset schedule)
- For monthly uptime below 99.9% and >= 99.0% but < 99.9% -> 10% monthly credit
- For monthly uptime below 99.0% and >= 95.0% -> 25% monthly credit

Estimated impact: the verified downtime yields an availability of ~99.51% for the billing month (approximation given current month totals). Under the schedule, the incident qualifies for a 10% monthly credit.

Proposed credit amount: 10% of $121,500 = $12,150.

Approval path: Finance can approve up to $15k operationally; any credit > $15k needs VP Finance sign-off. Credits > $10k also require a countersigned offset agreement (legal). Given this is ~$12.15k, we need: 1) Laura to prepare the offset agreement for signature; 2) Customer signature (DocuSign link can be used); 3) Finance will process the credit as an invoice offset applied to the next billing cycle once agreement is countersigned (processing time ~ 7-10 business days after countersignature).

I’ve attached a brief spreadsheet with the calculation and the exact windows used.

Markus Klein
Director, Revenue Operations (Finance)
